title: Constant bound for the maximum partial-cycle search factor
summary: Decide whether the maximum repeat-until factor in the partial-cycle de Bruijn search algorithm has an absolute constant upper bound.

formal_statement.body: With $q_d=|\mathcal F(d-1)|2^{\binom{n-1}{d}}/|\mathcal F(d)|$ and $q_{\max}(n)=\max_{0\le d\le n-1}q_d$, decide whether there is an absolute constant $C$ such that $q_{\max}(n)\le C$ for every admissible order $n$. Prove such a bound or prove that $q_{\max}(n)$ is unbounded.

scope.domain: Average repeat-until factors in the partial-cycle de Bruijn search algorithm
assumptions: $q_d$ and $\mathcal F(d)$ use the source's definitions
The bound $C$ must be independent of $n$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves only the loose exponential bound $q_{\max}(n)\le2^{n-2}-4$ and records empirical motivation for a fixed bound; no inspected later result proves boundedness or unboundedness.

citations.label: Li--Lin, fixed upper bound for q-max
citations.locator: Section VI, Algorithm 2 analysis, journal p. 606

progress.summary: The source notes that the product identity for the $q_d$ may indicate a fixed upper bound for $q_{\max}$ and leaves the quantified problem open.
